content.content:
# Climb batch 35: the judge's ruling on the merged-diff review

Decision: **repair**, of specification text and records only. One clause of an Appendix I effect is narrowed, and the FACTS entry and the gather's record line that restate it follow. No source, library, checker, interpreter or test file changes, so the gate does not run again: a repair reruns the gate only where it changes a path under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`, or `build.xml`, outside the test files, and `Specification/` and `explorations/` are not among those paths (`explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:1336-1337`, `gateReads`, applied by `repairRerun` at `:1452-1457`; the skill's `gate.md`, "When to run it"). The edit adds no example, so `ant testSpecData` (P-124) reads nothing it changes. It is not **land**: the settlement edits `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, and the land rule admits only tests and records.

The review's routed finding (review-routed.1, the test owed where rungs S and O meet, `PLAN.md:943`) goes to the next batch as the review routed it; I give it no ruling. The review's own record fixes (`b0a5943e76`, `explorations/` only) are not contested and stand. I did not read the gate's output.

## The finding, upheld

`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:6423-6425`, in the effect of the entry "The features not yet supported, in the preface and the introduction" (`\seclabel{revival-supported}`, `:6367`), reads: "the compiled type checker refuses an \KWD{override} in a generic trait over a declaration that the trait inherits under a \KWD{where} clause (row~1107)." The gather wrote it in O's commit `d56eb8a882` (its message: "the gather's correction"; `climb-batch-35/RECORD.md:131`).

The code refuses less than that:

- `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:384-385` extends the type analyzer with the trait's static parameters and `None`: a `where` clause of an `extends` entry is not held, so the clause's static parameter keeps its declared bound. Row 1107's note says the same: "The overloading check reads `A`'s `f` with `T` unbounded, the condition not held".
- `:410-411` reads what the trait provides, and which own declaration overrides which inherited one, on that analyzer (`STypesUtil.providedAndOverridden`). `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:1715-1716` pairs an `override` with an inherited declaration whose parameter types are equivalent to, or below, its own.
- `OverloadingChecker.scala:424` (`checkOverridesSomething`, `:755-789`) refuses an `override` that is in no pair.

So an inherited declaration whose parameter types do not name the clause's static parameter is read exactly, and an `override` over it is accepted. The reviewer's probe shows it on the merged code (`e922c2ea1a`): with `override g(x: Number)` in `G` over `A`'s `g(x: ZZ32)`, `bin/fortress typecheck` and `bin/fortress compile` exit 0 and `bin/fortress run` prints `G`; with `override f(x: ZZ32)` over `A`'s `f(x: T)` added, the checker refuses: 'Invalid override of f in trait G: (G[\T\], ZZ32)->String ... has the modifier override and does not override any inherited declaration.', 'Invalid overloading of f in trait G'. The sentence names every override over a declaration inherited under a `where` clause, so it is false of the first program.

The rule broken: an effect names each departure with its ledger row, so that "the text claims no more than holds" (the skill's `specification.md`, "When the text and an implementation disagree"; P-95, "Every change to the specification is recorded with its reason."). Row 1107's own claim names only the inherited declaration whose parameter type is the clause's static parameter.

## Which claims were right

- The reviewer: right that the clause is broader than the code and than row 1107's claim, and right that the repair needs no gate.
- The reviewer's suggested wording, "... and whose parameter type is that clause's static parameter (row~1107)", may still claim more than the code at one point. By `STypesUtil.scala:1716`, an `override` whose parameter type lies above the static parameter's declared bound, as `override f(x: Any)` over `f(x: T)` with `T` bounded by `Any`, is paired as an override even with the clause not held, so the checker would accept it. I ran nothing (my role runs no program); step 1 below settles it with one typecheck, and step 2 picks the wording by its result.
- The gather: wrong in `climb-batch-35/RECORD.md:131`, "each clause checked against `CodeGen.checkOverrideCompilable` ... and `OverloadingChecker.scala:410-411`, `:424`. Each states what the code does": the row-1107 clause did not. The same over-reach is in F-400 ("the checker refuses an override under a conditional extension that walk runs (row 1107)"), which the review did not name; it follows the repair, since FACTS binds later work.
- Rung O: its own records are exact. `rung-override-compiled/REPORT.md:84`, `:88` and `:134` and row 1107 name the one form tested.

## The repair

1. On the merged tree, with a private caches folder as the reviewer used, write and type check this program (`bin/fortress typecheck`, not `compile`: the code generator refuses an override over a declaration that names a static parameter, row 1106):

       component OverrideAboveBoundProbe
       export Executable
       trait A[\T\]
         f(x: T): String = "A"
       end
       trait G[\T\] extends A[\T\] where { T extends ZZ32 }
         override f(x: Any): String = "G"
       end
       object O extends G[\ZZ32\] end
       run(): () = println(O.f(3))
       end

   Keep it under your tree's `tmp/`. Quote its exit status and its first lines in your record. Exit 0 is outcome (a); 'Invalid override of f in trait G' is outcome (b).

2. `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:6423-6425`: replace the three lines

       the compiled type checker refuses an \KWD{override} in a generic trait over
       a declaration that the trait inherits under a \KWD{where} clause
       (row~1107).

   On outcome (a), with:

       the compiled type checker reads a declaration that a generic trait inherits
       under a \KWD{where} clause without that clause's bound, so it refuses an
       \KWD{override} that overrides the declaration only by that bound, as one
       whose parameter type is the bound over one whose parameter type is the
       clause's static parameter (row~1107).

   On outcome (b), with the reviewer's wording:

       the compiled type checker refuses an \KWD{override} in a generic trait over
       a declaration that the trait inherits under a \KWD{where} clause and whose
       parameter type is that clause's static parameter (row~1107).

   Change nothing else of the entry. The preface's item (`Specification/fortress/preamble.tex:87-88`, "\KWD{override} in compiled code where a static parameter is involved") holds and stays.

3. F-400 (`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:296`): with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py set`, replace only the clause "the checker refuses an override under a conditional extension that walk runs (row 1107)" with, on outcome (a), "the checker refuses an override that overrides a declaration inherited under a conditional extension only by the clause's bound, which walk runs (row 1107)", or on outcome (b), "the checker refuses an override over a declaration inherited under a conditional extension whose parameter type is the clause's static parameter, which walk runs (row 1107)". Commit `FACTS.md` and `FACTS-history.md` together.

4. On outcome (a) only, row 1107 (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:572`): with `ledger.py rewrite 1107 FILE`, replace in its claim "over the inherited declaration whose parameter type is the clause's static parameter" with "over an inherited declaration that it overrides only by the clause's bound", keeping the example and every other cell. The row is at 1,179 of 1,200 characters; the new words are shorter. Add no note. On outcome (b), leave the row.

5. `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-35/RECORD.md:131`: after "Each states what the code does, so neither is a text mismatch.", add one sentence: the row-1107 clause stated more than the code, and the review's repair narrowed it (this file; the repair's commit). Leave `PLAN.md:939`, whose "the checker's refusal under a conditional extension (row 1107)" names the refusal, not its reach.

6. Build the specification once, on the text after step 2, as the repair's brief and the skill's `specification.md`, "Building it", say, and only after the gate running in this tree has ended. Both commands must end in `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` and the warnings grep must print 0. Keep the PDF where the repair's brief says, then `git clean -fXq -- Specification`.

7. Run no gate, no suite and no stage: nothing that the gate reads changed. Commit the paths of steps 2 to 5 with the skill's footer, saying that the commit edits the original tree (`Specification/`).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# spend.py <since-epoch> <file-or-dir>...: tokens written (input + cache creation) and read, per transcript, deduplicated by message id
# the coordinating session's own transcript (fe616d40) is left out; agents: <session-dir>/subagents/*.jsonl or a task output file; claude -p runs: the project directory
import json, os, sys, glob
since=float(sys.argv[1]); files=[]
for a in sys.argv[2:]:
    files += [a] if os.path.isfile(a) else glob.glob(os.path.join(a,'*.jsonl'))
tw=tr=0; n=0
for f in sorted(set(files)):
    if os.path.getmtime(f) < since or os.path.basename(f).startswith("fe616d40"): continue
    seen={}; 
    for line in open(f, errors='replace'):
        try: r=json.loads(line)
        except Exception: continue
        m=r.get('message') if isinstance(r.get('message'),dict) else None
        if not m or 'usage' not in m: continue
        seen[m.get('id') or id(m)]=m['usage']
    w=sum(u.get('input_tokens',0)+u.get('cache_creation_input_tokens',0) for u in seen.values())
    rd=sum(u.get('cache_read_input_tokens',0) for u in seen.values())
    if seen: n+=1; tw+=w; tr+=rd; print(f"{os.path.basename(f)[:40]:40} calls={len(seen):4} written={w/1e3:8.1f}K read={rd/1e6:6.2f}M")
print(f"TOTAL files={n} written={tw/1e6:.2f}M read={tr/1e6:.2f}M")

import json,sys,glob,os,re
W=sys.argv[1]
for f in sorted(glob.glob(W+'/agent-*.jsonl')):
    lab=json.load(open(f[:-6]+'.meta.json')).get('description','')
    users=[]
    for line in open(f,errors='replace'):
        try: r=json.loads(line)
        except Exception: continue
        m=r.get('message') if isinstance(r.get('message'),dict) else None
        if r.get('type')=='user' and m:
            c=m.get('content')
            if isinstance(c,str): users.append((r.get('timestamp'),c))
            elif isinstance(c,list):
                t=''.join(x.get('text','') for x in c if isinstance(x,dict) and x.get('type')=='text')
                if t: users.append((r.get('timestamp'),t))
        if len(users)>=3: break
    print('##',lab,os.path.basename(f)[6:14], 'user text msgs seen:',len(users))
    for ts,t in users[:3]:
        has='facts-extract' in t
        nkeys=len(re.findall(r"'(?:P-\d+|F-\d+|ledger:\d+|doc:[^']+|code:[^']+|map:[^']+)'|\"(?:P-\d+|F-\d+|ledger:\d+|doc:[^\"]+|code:[^\"]+|map:[^\"]+)\"",t))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# calls.py FILE: each tool call in order: index, assistant-message index, seconds after the first record, tool, input (first 300 chars), result chars, is_error
import json, sys
from datetime import datetime
def ts(s):
    try: return datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace('Z','+00:00')).timestamp()
    except Exception: return None
def calls(f):
    t0=None; out=[]; byid={}; amsg=0; lastmid=None
    for line in open(f, errors='replace'):
        try: r=json.loads(line)
        except Exception: continue
        t=ts(r.get('timestamp','')) if isinstance(r.get('timestamp'),str) else None
        if t and t0 is None: t0=t
        m=r.get('message') if isinstance(r.get('message'),dict) else None
        if not m: continue
        c=m.get('content')
        if r.get('type')=='assistant':
            mid=m.get('id')
            if mid!=lastmid: amsg+=1; lastmid=mid
            if isinstance(c,list):
                for x in c:
                    if x.get('type')=='tool_use':
                        d={'i':len(out)+1,'msg':amsg,'t':(t-t0) if t and t0 else None,'abs':t,'tool':x.get('name'),'input':x.get('input'),'rchars':0,'err':False,'rtext':''}
                        out.append(d); byid[x.get('id')]=d
        elif r.get('type')=='user' and isinstance(c,list):
            for x in c:
                if x.get('type')=='tool_result':
                    d=byid.get(x.get('tool_use_id'))
                    if not d: continue
                    cc=x.get('content')
                    if isinstance(cc,list): s=''.join(y.get('text','') for y in cc if isinstance(y,dict))
                    else: s=str(cc or '')
                    d['rchars']=len(s); d['err']=bool(x.get('is_error')); d['rtext']=s
    return out
if __name__=='__main__':
    for d in calls(sys.argv[1]):
        inp=d['input']; s=inp.get('command') if isinstance(inp,dict) and 'command' in inp else json.dumps(inp)
        print(d['i'], d['msg'], round(d['t'] or 0), d['tool'], d['rchars'], 'ERR' if d['err'] else '', (s or '')[:300].replace('\n',' | '))

== explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md, ## The harness and the gate

FACTS.md:207
- F-354 **Two compiles of one source by different builds of the compiler need not give the same bytes, so a comparison of jars cannot show that a change left the compiled code as it was.** The code generator writes a class's methods and a dispatch method's tests in an order that follows the JVM's identity hashes (row 996). Two cold compiles of the prelude by one build give equal classes, 590 of 590, because the default identity hash is the same sequence in each run. Under another hash mode 18 of `CompilerBuiltin`'s 312 classes differ: the same methods in another order. So the tests, not the bytes, show that a change of the compiler left the prelude undisturbed, and a result that depends on the order can come and go between builds. Measured once, on `832f7d0d91`'s code. Detail: `compile-ladder/plan-31/probes/probe-y.md`, "6. A finding beside the question: the prelude's jars change with any change of the compiler".

== explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md, ## The checker and the one library

FACTS.md:106
- F-232 **The syntax tree's hashes do not depend on the JVM's identity hashes, except at inference variables, walk's wrapped values and the nodes that hold them.** Every generated node's hash starts from the hash of its class's name: makeAST's post-processing of ASTGen's output writes that start, and so do the in-repo generators (`build.xml:698-716`). A field whose type holds an `Option` is hashed by `NodeHash.of` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeHash.java`), since the PLT `Option` classes hash by identity. So hash maps and sets of nodes that hold neither exception iterate in one order whatever code asked for an identity hash before, and so do the apis that `StaticChecker.checkApis` takes in turn. The exceptions hash through identity hashes: an inference variable's id is a bare `Object` (`nodes_util/NodeFactory.java:1166-1184`), but no output of the count stage moves through its hash; walk's `_WrappedFValue` hashes its `FValue` by walk's own hash, which can be an identity hash (`interpreter/evaluator/_WrappedFValue.java:170-177`; row 430). `DeclaredFunction`s, entries of the checker's index and not nodes, still hash by identity, but since row 737's repair no choice of `ApiTypeExtractor` depends on their order (F-254). Gated by `NodeHashJUTest`, and row 737's repair by `OmittedReturnTypeFromApi`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-ast-hashes/REPORT.md` sections 4.2 to 4.4.

content.content:
## For the curator

A dead end is a store that takes items in and has no working way to let them out.

One cause is behind most of them. Each landing runs a workflow that writes into six stores for you. Nothing but your word takes an item out. The workflow writes about 17 queue items and 11 page items a day. You answered about 3 queue items and read about 3 page items a day. The stores can only grow.

The landing's bookkeeping also costs more than the batch. Climb batch 34b's run wrote 2.0M tokens. The landing work before it wrote 4.1M.

The dead ends, in order of what they cost you:

1. **The review queue.** In 16 days, 266 items went in and about 64 went out. 185 of the 270 open items are defaults that a batch already landed. They are news, not questions.
   - Fix: a landed default is closed when it lands. You get one short report for each landing that says what changed in the language. Only a real question enters the queue, with the work that waits for it.
   - This is your "1" of today, taken one step further: the queue stops holding landed defaults at all. It needs your yes.
2. **The page of `fortress-repo` changes.** It got 172 new items in 16 days. You read 41. Most items are a sentence brought in line with the tree, not a new rule.
   - Fix: the page shows only a new rule or a changed rule. Every other change is one line with its commit. An item leaves at the next landing whether you read it or not.
   - It gives up your sight of each wording change of the worker skill. It needs your yes.
3. **The same item in up to six files.** A waiting item is copied into the batch's record, PLAN's review list, the queue's body, the queue's head, a docket and the boot note. The copies drift. On 11-17 a stale copy made the coordinator ask you a closed question (item 513).
   - Fix: one home for a question. PLAN's 37 review lists and the queue's head section go. A new sort edits the queue; it does not write a new file.
   - It needs your yes, since it changes the review list.
4. **A defect becomes a skill sentence, not a fix.** The landing workflow tells the skill writer to add a sentence for each new trap. Nothing tells a planner to fix the row. Open ledger rows went from 489 to 553 in 18 days. The worker skill grew by a quarter.
   - Fix: P-180, which you decided today, plus three mechanics: the writer adds no trap sentence; the planner gives each rung the open rows of the files that it edits; closing a row lists the skill lines to delete.
   - One point is yours: which rows P-180 binds. Options are below.
5. **Nothing teaches you what landed.** The cleanup of 11-05 wrote 117 landed decisions as "material for a page that he reads". The page was never built. You said on 11-10 that you are not learning much yet.
   - Fix: the landing report of fix 1 is that channel. It replaces the learning file.
   - It is part of fix 1.
6. **Sorts and reviews that end as a file.** The docket of 11-15 found 99 items to close and 11 contradictions. Eight days later they are still in the boot note as owed.
   - Fix: a worker that sorts a store edits the store, on a branch, as today's triage does. The coordinator lands the branch.
   - The coordinator's own change.
7. **The boot note's lists of owed work.** Some lines are 30 days old. The note is for state, and it has no step that does the work.
   - Fix: owed work goes to one housekeeping list. A housekeeping worker empties it at each landing. A line that survives two landings is done or dropped, with one line to you.
   - This is the housekeeping batch that you asked for today. The coordinator's own change.
8. **The held list.** It holds 80K characters and is read at every boot. A line leaves only at a trim.
   - Fix: each line names its exit when it is written: a decision in POSITIONS, a task for the skill writer, or an answer in chat. The line leaves when that happens.
   - It needs your yes, since it changes the held list.
9. **Stores that only cost tokens.** The skill's `sources.md` (357K) is larger than the skill. FACTS (403K) is read whole after a boot. PLAN's "Where we stand" is 15K in five bullets.
   - Fix: provenance goes in the commit message; FACTS is read by query; "Where we stand" is rewritten short at each landing.
   - The coordinator's own change.

One finding would change a decision of yours: P-180's scope (finding 4). Four fixes change how you and the coordinator work, and wait for your yes: 1 (with 5), 2, 3 and 8. The rest are the coordinator's.

## The findings, sorted by what each needs

### A. Would change a decision of the curator's: an ask, with options

**A1. Which rows P-180 binds (finding 4).** P-180 says that "a batch fixes the defects that make walk and the compiled path behave differently or depart from the specification". 553 rows are open, and a batch opens about 20 and closes about 14 beside its main work (208 opened and 138 fixed in 18 days). The entry does not say which of them a batch takes, so a planner cannot tell when the rule is met. The inventory (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/skill-workarounds.md`) counts 98 skill passages whose fix needs no decision, 17 of them with no row yet.

1. By the files in hand: each rung fixes the open rows that cite the files it edits and need no decision, or says in its report why one stays. The planner lists them in the rung's section. Costs each rung some of its budget; reaches every area in time; needs no extra batch.
2. By the skill: only the 98 passages of the inventory, in housekeeping batches, until the skill teaches no workaround. Then P-180 is met. Bounded and countable; leaves the 400 rows that no passage names as they are.
3. By a balance: a batch may not open more rows than it closes. The strongest reading; it can stop a batch that finds many defects, which punishes finding them.

How they weigh: 2 ends the symptom that he met and stops there; 1 changes the planning for good at a small cost per rung; 3 turns a measure into a gate. Recommendation: 2 first, as the housekeeping batch already in planning, and 1 as the standing rule after it; report 3's balance at each landing and gate nothing on it.

### B. Change how the curator and the coordinator work: for his yes to the exact words

**B1. The review queue holds landed defaults as open items (dead ends 1 and 5).**

- Enters: at each landing, the sorter and the routing writer file every fork taken at a default, every reserved point reached, every difference that the gate's comparison hid, every rewritten line of a team test (`batch.md`, "The checker count and the distance", "Reserved points and repairs"; `sort.md`: "A default that the coordinator or a batch took is not his answer: that item stays open").
- Kept: the queue's body, its head section, PLAN's review list.
- Consumed: by the curator, one per message (`SKILL.md`, way 2: "Put it to the curator later, one per message").
- Exit: his word on that item. In 16 days, 3 items left as "reviewed by him as landed".
- Cost: his attention and trust (his words of 11-02 and of today); wrong asks from stale copies (B3); about 1.6M tokens a landing for the record step; and the real questions, 8 on 11-15, are hidden among 200.

(* A numeral with a radix point counts its leading zeros among its digits: a coercion over its four numbers reads three digits for 00.5. *)
component RadixPointLeadingZerosWalk
export Executable

object Digits(count: ZZ32)
  coerce[\nat n, nat m, nat r, nat v\](x: RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]) = Digits(n.asZZ32)
end

counted(d: Digits): ZZ32 = d.count

run(): () = do
    assert(counted(00.5), 3, "literals.tex, section \"Literals\": 00.5 has three digits")
    println "PASS"
  end

end
(* A numeral with a radix point counts its leading zeros among its digits: a compiled coercion over its four numbers reads three digits for 00.5. *)
component RadixPointLeadingZerosCompiled
export Executable

value object Digits(count: ZZ32)
  coerce[\nat n, nat m, nat r, nat v\](x: RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]) = Digits(bigToZZ64(n).asZZ32)
end

counted(d: Digits): ZZ32 = d.count

run(): () = do
  assert(counted(00.5), 3, "literals.tex, section \"Literals\": 00.5 has three digits")
  assert(counted(0.5), 2, "0.5 has two digits")
  println("PASS")
end

bigToZZ64(z: ZZ): ZZ64 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.bigOverflowingToLong")
end

- A numeral with a radix point keeps only one of its leading zeros, so a coercion over `RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]` gets `n` = 2 for `00.5`, not 3 (ledger row 960).
---
- A superscript is `^` and what follows it, as the exponent in `x^2` or the transpose `^T`. It can follow a dotted access: `p.wq^T` is `(p.wq)^T`. After a call or a subscript, parenthesise first, as `(f(x))^T` and `(x[5])^2`: `f(x)^T` is a static error, and `x[5]^2` compiles, but under walk fails or gives the wrong element (ledger row 1).
---
Walk also departs from the rules at these bindings:

- The right side of a top-level tuple binding runs once for each name and once more: `(first, second) = pairOnce()` runs `pairOnce` three times (ledger row 1026). Bind the call to one name, as `pair = pairOnce()`, then write `(first, second) = pair`.
- A `var` declared in a block with an array type and bound to an array literal, as `var t: ZZ32[2] = [5 6]`, is immutable: 'Cannot assign to immutable t' (ledger row 1024). Bind the literal to an immutable name, and initialize the `var` from it.
---
  - At a place that fixes a type (`revival-changes.md`, "Numbers"), the checker refuses an atomic expression whose value is a numeral, as `atomic if c then 1 else 0 end`, and `atomic 1` fails the JVM's verification (ledger row 1043). Write `atomic do ... end`.
- An `exit` that runs after its `label` block has completed, from a function made in the block, ends a compiled program with the Java exception `LabelExit`, which no `catch` clause takes. Under walk, a `catch` clause of the library's `LabelException` takes it. The rules do not settle which is right (ledger row 1041).
- Where an object overloads an inherited functional method by declarations of its own, and `self` is not the first parameter, the compiled dispatch method tests the receiver's type where it should test the other argument's. A call then dies with `ClassCastException` (ledger row 573). Where the receiver has the parameter type of one of the object's own declarations, the call runs that declaration whatever the argument (ledger row 1038). Put `self` first in such overloads.
- On the compiled path, two `value` objects with a `var` field, built alike, are not strictly equivalent: `V(1) === V(1)` is `false` (ledger row 112).
---
It also refuses a function or method with a contract (`requires`, `ensures`, `invariant`). It compiles a declaration whose own header or `extends` entry has a `where` clause, and emits nothing for the clause. A call of a function or method whose own clause introduces a `where`-clause variable, as `where [\nat n\]` does, links, but dies at run time with `NoClassDefFoundError` (ledger row 867). `compiler_tests/XXXWhereVariableCallCompiled.test` records it: copy its form for such a call. The disambiguator, which both paths run, drops a trait's or object's contract, so the code generator never sees one, and walk does not check one either (ledger row 781). It refuses a function or method with a modifier other than `getter`, `setter`, `io`, `private`, `abstract` and `test`, such as `override` (ledger row 650). A trait or object that extends a generic trait compiles with `Any` as the static argument. With `Bottom`, `Self` or an abbreviated type there, the code generator refuses the declaration. An abbreviated type is a short form, such as `RR64[3]` for an array type. With a tuple that holds `Any` there, the code generator crashes (ledger row 889).
---
126:An `exit` out of an `atomic` block loses the block's writes, on both paths (ledger row 1039). Set a flag in the block, and exit after the block.

# Rung W, the judge's ruling: the skeptic's fix of the tuple binding's numerals

One launch of the judge worked this rung. Head judged: `83e4cbf432`. One fix was contested, `675932404d`; this ruling covers it and nothing else. No build and no test ran for this ruling: it reads the branch, the record, the specification and the code.

## Decision

**Stands.** `675932404d` is upheld; nothing is reverted. The rung lands as the branch holds it. One residue of the fix lands unrepaired and goes to the curator (below, "What lands unrepaired").

## The fix

`DesugarerVisitor.forVarDecl` now binds a tuple binding in two ways (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/rewrite/DesugarerVisitor.java`):

- a right side that is a tuple expression of as many elements as names, with no varargs and no keywords, becomes one declaration per name, each initialized by its own element, with no temporary (`:868-877`);
- any other right side is bound once to the temporary, now declared at the tuple of the names' types, `Any` for an untyped name, or untyped when no name has a type (`:878-893`), and each name reads its element from it through the worker's `Member` or `Local` reference (`:895-903`).

Its test, `ProjectFortress/tests/TupleBindingNumeralTypesWalk.fss`, failed on the worker's head (SKEPTIC.md, "Finding 1"):

    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh <tree>/tmp/.../h1 ProjectFortress/tests/TupleBindingNumeralTypesWalk.fss
    # harness-one 2026-11-23T11:38:25Z; tree 9e3a47ac20; nproc=4; ...
    Type mismatch binding 5: ZZ32 (type ZZ32) to un (type NN32)
    Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0

## Which claims were right

**The skeptic.**

1. Right: the worker's change was a defect against a decision on record. On the worker's head the temporary was untyped (`DesugarerVisitor.java:868` at `9e3a47ac20`). A top-level cell makes every numeral of its value plain, at its default (`interpreter/env/LazilyEvaluatedCell.java:76`, `theValue = Numerals.plain(v)`, which goes into a tuple: `interpreter/evaluator/values/Numerals.java:250-257`), so `(u: NN32, r: RR32) = (5, 0.5)` reached `u` as a `ZZ32` and stopped. The specification converts a numeral where the declared type of a variable or a field fixes one, "\EXP{n\COLON\mathbb{N}32 = 5} the natural number 5" (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:199-208`), and P-173 binds walk to it: "walk converts from the exact value at the same places, place by place". A field has the top-level declaration's meanings (`Specification/basic/objects.tex:295-297`), so the object form is the same defect. The base bound each of these (SKEPTIC.md's table).
2. Right: a temporary at the names' types for every right side, the way that keeps W2's wording, refuses `(arr, n): (ZZ32[2], ZZ32) = ([1 2], 3)`, which the base runs. The mechanism is in the code: a cell builds an array literal only where it is the cell's whole value (`LazilyEvaluatedCell.java:71-74`), and `Coercions.coerceTuple` converts a tuple's elements by coercion alone (`interpreter/evaluator/values/Coercions.java:317-334`).
3. Right, and stronger than the skeptic put it: the split follows the team's own code. The checker has the same two cases. For a tuple expression of as many elements as names, it checks each element at its own name's declared type (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Decls.scala:250-277`). For any other right side, it checks the whole at the tuple of the declared types (`Decls.scala:280-300`, "Gather declared types of LHS as a big tuple type"). The skeptic cited `:272-277` for the second case, but those lines end the first one. The slip changes no part of the argument. The team's code generator likewise binds a field's tuple expression element by element (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5312-5318`).
4. Understated: the residue is a regression against the base, not only against the worker's head (below).

**The worker.**

1. Right: the fix departs from fork W2's wording for one shape. W2 reads "Each name of a top-level tuple binding reads its element from the temporary, so the right side runs once" (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:448`), and a tuple expression no longer has a temporary.
2. Right: decision 3, the reference built by the desugarer's `Member` or `Local` rewriter, still stands. It serves every right side that is not a tuple expression (`DesugarerVisitor.java:897`).
3. Wrong as a ground for a revert. The rung's section says of its decisions, "None names the mechanism" (`CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:494`). A fork "chooses where the record leaves an implementation open" (`CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:442`). W2's purpose clause, that the right side runs once, still holds: each element of the tuple expression is evaluated once, in the one declaration that it initializes. Against W2's wording stand the specification and P-173, and the specification is the standard (POSITIONS.md, P-25). A revert would land the refusal above for every typed tuple binding of a numeral at a non-default type: `(u: NN32, r: RR32) = (5, 0.5)`, `(un, uq): (NN32, QQ) = (5, 0.1)`, `(en, em): NN32... = (7, 8)`, the `var` form and the field form. A program meets that form more often than any form that the fix leaves refused.

## What lands unrepaired

After the fix, a typed tuple binding stops at load where four things hold together:

- its right side is not a tuple expression of as many elements as names;
- an array literal is written inside that right side;
- the literal is bound to a name declared at an array type;
- the binding is a top-level variable or a field.

An example is `(arr, n): (ZZ32[2], ZZ32) = if flag then ([4 5], 6) else ([7 8], 9) end`.

The base ran it. On the base each name's initializer was the right side's own field at the name's declared type (`DesugarerVisitor.java:872-874` at `13f4fdea75`), and that cell built the literal (`LazilyEvaluatedCell.java:71-74`). The skeptic's correction says so in its message (`git show f39d01a66a`):

    NEW-W-2: under walk an array literal in a
    tuple bound at a tuple type is not built, for a variable on the base and now
    for a tuple binding over an if (tests/XXXTypedTupleArrayLiteralWalk).

SKEPTIC.md calls the failure new only "against the worker's head" ("Failure modes"). In fact it is new against the base too. It is walk's existing gap in typed tuples, row 1105, which the base shows for `t: (ZZ32[2], ZZ32) = ([1 2], 3)`. The fix now reaches the same gap from a tuple binding: walk reads that binding as the checker does, as a binding at the tuple type (`Decls.scala:280-300`). The branch records the gap. It has a row in record.md, the XXX test `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXTypedTupleArrayLiteralWalk.fss`, and a workaround: bind the array to a name of its own.

A second output changes. Where a typed tuple binding's right side is not a tuple expression and does not convert, the message names the temporary, 'Type mismatch binding (5,6) ... to *tuple_<span> (type (NN32,String))' (SKEPTIC.md, "Failure modes"). On the base it named the variable.

**Why not a repair round.** Each way that removes the residue edits a file outside the rung's section. The section's files are `Evaluator.java`, `DesugarerVisitor.java`, the tests and row 152. Each way also changes how every walk binding converts its value:

- (a) `Coercions.coerceTuple` builds an array literal at an array element type, as `LazilyEvaluatedCell.java:71-74` does through `LHSEvaluator.topLevelArray`. This also repairs row 1105's variable form.
- (b) The temporary keeps its value raw, and each name converts its own element. Walk's local tuple binding works this way already: `interpreter/evaluator/BuildLetEnvironments.java:103-118` evaluates the right side once and binds each element through `LHSEvaluator`. This way needs `LazilyEvaluatedCell.java:76` and the field initializer to skip `Numerals.plain` for the temporary: the skeptic's way (d).

The residue is narrow and recorded, and both ways stay open, so the rung lands now and the residue goes to the curator.

## Points this ruling adds

- A decision taken where nothing on record settles it: a narrow regression against the base lands, the `if` form above, rather than a repair beyond the rung's files. The ways are (a) and (b) above.
- Reserved point, an interpreter output that changed: the residue and the message above, beside those in REPORT.md, "Points to report", 6.

Neither is a step that cannot be undone, nor one against a decision on record. Neither holds the push.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# runs3.py RUN_DIR LABEL_RE: the build, suite and stage commands (their core) of matching agents
import json, sys, os, re, glob
d=sys.argv[1]; lre=re.compile(sys.argv[2])
core=re.compile(r"(ant [a-zA-Z]+[^;&|']*|checker-count/run\.sh[^;&|']*|distance/run\.sh[^;&|']*|count-run[^;&|']*|git (rev-parse|log -1|stash|checkout|switch)[^;&|']*|harness-one\.sh[^;&|']{0,80}|junit\.sh[^;&|']{0,80}|fortress compile [^;&|']{0,60})")
def lab(f):
    try: return json.load(open(f[:-6]+'.meta.json'))['description']
    except Exception: return '?'
for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d,'agent-*.jsonl'))):
    L=lab(f)
    if not lre.search(L): continue
    print('##',L)
    seen=set()
    for line in open(f,errors='replace'):
        try: r=json.loads(line)
        except Exception: continue
        m=r.get('message')
        if not isinstance(m,dict) or m.get('role')!='assistant': continue
        for c in m.get('content') or []:
            if isinstance(c,dict) and c.get('type')=='tool_use' and c.get('name')=='Bash':
                cmd=' '.join(c['input'].get('command','').split())
                if c.get('id') in seen: continue
                seen.add(c.get('id'))
                hits=[x.group(0)[:110] for x in core.finditer(cmd) if not x.group(0).startswith('ant -') ]
                hits=[h for h in hits if re.match(r'ant (compileAll|clean|test|tex|genSource)|checker-count|distance|count-run|harness|junit|fortress compile|git (stash|checkout|switch)',h)]
                if hits:
                    print(' ', r.get('timestamp','')[11:19], ' | '.join(hits)[:300])

A self-typed trait is a trait `C[\X\]` whose parameter `X` extends `C[\X\]`. The Return Type check reads `self` as `C[\X\] & X` in the trait's signature where an object's dotted method redeclares the trait's method at the same parameter types, so it refuses a narrower return type; a getter so redeclared reads the plain type and compiles (F-394). That reading of a dotted method departs from P-146 and P-157, which keep the plain signatures for the Return Type Rule (row 1094). The checker also takes a parameter bounded by a self-typed trait that the trait extends at that parameter, as the team's `Containment` mixins are: a default of the coordinator's. In a trait whose `comprises` clause lists types, `self` is instead the trait met with the union of those types, and the exclusion test reads its signatures plain. (* A trait that comprises one object, with a getter that calls the trait's abstract functional methods on self, compiles to default methods that load, the calls taking the trait's own declarations. *)
component ComprisesSelfAbstractFunctionalMethodCall
export Executable

trait Solid comprises { Brick }
    getter total(): ZZ32 = width(self) + height(self) + depth(self) + mass(self)
    getter kind(): String = "solid"
    width(self): ZZ32
    height(self): ZZ32
    depth(self): ZZ32
    mass(self): ZZ32
end

object Brick(w: ZZ32, h: ZZ32, d: ZZ32, m: ZZ32) extends Solid
    width(self): ZZ32 = w
    height(self): ZZ32 = h
    depth(self): ZZ32 = d
    mass(self): ZZ32 = m
end

run(): () = do
    s: Solid = Brick(1, 20, 300, 4000)
    assert(s.kind, "solid", "Solid's default methods load")
    println("PASS")
  end

end
# A trait that comprises one object, with a getter that calls the trait's abstract functional methods on self, compiles to default methods that load.
tests=ComprisesSelfAbstractFunctionalMethodCall
compile
link
run
run_out_contains=PASS
(* An object's methods with the modifier override widen the parameter of the ones they override, so its calls run them and print f PASS and g PASS (traits.tex, section "Method Declarations"). *)
component OverrideModifierCodeGeneration
export Executable

trait A
  f(self, other:ZZ32):String = "f FAIL"
  g(other:ZZ32):String = "g FAIL"
end

object B extends A
  override f(self, other:Number):String = "f PASS"
  override g(other:Number):String = "g PASS"
end

run():() = do
    println(f(B, 17))
    println(B.g(17))
  end

end
(* The right side of a top-level tuple binding is evaluated once (variables.tex, section "Top-Level Variable Declarations"). *)
component TopLevelTupleBindingOnceWalk
export Executable

var calls: ZZ32 = 0
(first, second) = pairOnce()

pairOnce(): (ZZ32, ZZ32) = do
    calls += 1
    (calls, 10 calls)
end

run(): () = do
    assert(calls, 1, "the right side ran once")
    assert(first, 1, "first")
    assert(second, 10, "second")
end

end

content.content:
A tie that self's type makes in a trait that comprises an object keeps the trait's own declaration, free of the identity-hash order

Climb batch 35's gate repair (row 1100). The checker reads self in a trait whose comprises clause lists types as the trait met with them, and reads the trait's own self parameter the same way, so a call such as denominator(self) in QQ ties QQ's declaration and Ratio's. The tie kept the first candidate in the overloadings' identity-hash order, so the one library's QQ default methods compiled the call at Ratio's arrow in ant's onelibrary JVM and failed verification, which turned the gate red (fast-onelibrary, 40 tests, 9 failures). The tie now keeps the candidates that take self at its trait's type: the call compiles at QQ's arrow and dispatch reaches Ratio's body.

New compiled test ComprisesSelfAbstractFunctionalMethodCall; ant testOneLibrary 40 tests, 0 failures; the S and O tests 22 of 22. Row 1100 rewritten as traced, to close after this commit; row 996 noted; the gate judge's three items for the curator in PLAN.md; REPAIR-gate.md records the steps and the deviations from the ruling. Edits the original tree.
